summary: C6 is the palace's philosophy-register neighborhood — Stoicism and Confucianism as the load-bearing hubs, Deleuze/Whitehead/Merleau-Ponty/Spinoza/Leibniz as the concept-philosophers, Dialectic/Excellent Adventure/Philosopher Visits the Entry/STIGMERGY Philosophical Lenses/The Lens as the practices that circulate them, and a small roster of Stoic and dialogic-philosophy persons (Epictetus, Marcus Aurelius, Seneca, Martin Buber, Martin Heidegger). It is already extremely densely cross-linked internally (Palace Philosophies alone is reached by 28) — the folders were not, in fact, blind to most of the cross-domain links here; the room had already found them. Two genuine things this pass turned up: first, Martin Heidegger and Martin Buber sit in the same room, share a named critic (Levinas, cited on both pages for opposite reasons), and stake out exactly opposed positions on the other person — Heidegger's Dasein "treats other people mostly as 'the they'" while Buber's whole philosophy is "there is no I as such, only the I of I-Thou and the I of I-It" — yet the two pages have never been linked to each other. Second, and the best find of the room: The Adjacent Affordance's "Symposium" section voices seven of this room's philosophers by name in body prose (Epictetus, Spinoza, Confucius, Leibniz, Whitehead, Merleau-Ponty, Deleuze) as a genuine fictional-but-honest device ("the attribution names the lens, not the mouth"), and none of those seven names carry a frontmatter link on that page — a clean, unforced unsung-paths harvest. Outside the room, the newcomer Iain McGilchrist (reached by only 6) is a strong, non-generic match for this neighborhood on two fronts: his right-hemisphere "comprehends the living whole... lets the world presence before it is broken into parts" is close kin to Merleau-Ponty's pre-reflective body-schema grasp of a living whole (not computed, not represented), and his whole forward vector — "what kind of attention are you paying to this" — is literally the shape of a roster candidate for Philosopher Visits the Entry, which already runs a "starting roster" of which voice visits which family of entry.

typed_relations.label: they-vs-thou
typed_relations.evidence: Heidegger: 'I have almost no ethics and almost no account of other people as anything but "the they"' / Buber: 'there is no I as such, only the I of I-Thou and the I of I-It... Through the Thou a person becomes I.'
typed_relations.rationale: Both pages are in the room and both explicitly stage the same critic (Levinas) against them for opposite reasons — Levinas breaks with Heidegger for having no ethics-first account of the other, and breaks with Buber for making the meeting too symmetrical to carry Levinas's asymmetric obligation. The two pages name exactly opposed treatments of das Man/the impersonal mass versus the I-Thou meeting, but have never been linked to each other. Fidelity check: swapping in, say, Epictetus for Buber doesn't produce the same specific opposition — Epictetus's quarrel with Heidegger (already linked, contradicts The Dichotomy of Control) is about control/thrownness, a different axis entirely.

typed_relations.label: comprehending-not-representing
typed_relations.evidence: Merleau-Ponty: 'You do not navigate the world by computing the position of your limbs; your body has a pre-reflective, operative grasp of itself' / McGilchrist: 'The right pays broad, open, sustained, vigilant attention; it comprehends — grasps the living whole in context... lets the world presence before it is broken into parts,' against the left hemisphere which 'abstracts, categorizes, and re-presents.'
typed_relations.rationale: Both name the same structure from different disciplines: skilled/comprehending cognition is a direct, pre-reflective grasp of a living whole, and the reductive move (computing/representing, or the left hemisphere's re-presentation) is what destroys it. McGilchrist is a priority newcomer (reached by only 6) and this is not generic — swap in Deleuze for McGilchrist and the specific embodied-attention register doesn't hold the same way (Deleuze's difference-in-itself is metaphysical, not about attention as a felt, bodily act).

typed_relations.label: attention-as-the-question
typed_relations.evidence: Philosopher Visits the Entry: 'a starting roster of which voice visits which family' — 'This is a seed, not a law.' McGilchrist: 'I earn my place by being dispatched to where a thing is about to be killed by the wrong kind of attention... I want to keep asking what kind of attention the palace is paying.'
typed_relations.rationale: The roster entry is explicitly open to growing ('a seed, not a law'), and McGilchrist's entire forward_vector is written in exactly the register of a roster candidate — a characteristic question that bites on entries that reduce a living whole to its analyzed parts. This wires an under-reached newcomer's inbound link through the room's own practice for doing exactly that.
